 KUALA LUMPUR: The flood situation in Perak and Selangor continues to improve Saturday (Nov 21) afternoon, with the total number of evacuees decreasing to 2,334 people from 683 families, down from 2,368 people from 691 families in the morning while the situation in Negri Sembilan has fully recovered.
 In PERAK, the number of flood evacuees across five districts has dropped to 488 people from 166 families, currently sheltered in six temporary evacuation centres (PPS), compared to 499 people from 169 families this morning.
 The State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) secretariat reported that one evacuation centre at SK Dato' Sagor in the Perak Tengah district, housing 22 evacuees was fully closed at 3pm Saturday while, SK Tanjung Belanja remains in operation, sheltering 70 evacuees from 35 families.
 Apart from that, the number of evacuees at the SRAR Padang Serai evacuation centre in Manjung remains at 131 people from 39 families, while the Teluk Intan Municipal Council Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak is sheltering 97 people from 31 families and in the Larut, Matang, and Selama district, 10 people from four families remain sheltered at the SK Batu Hampar evacuation centre.
 In Kerian, 180 evacuees from 57 families including 12 people from three families affected by a landslide remain housed at the SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman evacuation centres.
 In SELANGOR, the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) 'InfoBencana' portal reports that the number of evacuees has decreased slightly to 1,846 people from 517 families, compared to 1,869 people from 522 families this morning.
 The temporary evacuation centre (PPS) at SK Dato' Maharaja Lela is housing the highest number of evacuees, with 401 people, followed by SK Parit Mahang (365), SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (222), SRA Bukit Kuching (216), the Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (139), SK Rantau Panjang (134), and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (120).
 Also in operation are the PPS at SK Jaya Setia, which is housing 98 evacuees, Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (66), the Seri Harmoni Community Hall (40), SK Batu Arang (25), and the Kampung Sungai Kelambu Village Hall (20).
 Meanwhile, in NEGERI SEMBILAN, the state's Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) reported that the PPS at SK Jimah was fully closed at 2pm Saturday, following a complete improvement in the flood situation.
 However, the Malaysian Meteorological Department's weather forecast anticipates that some areas in the state will experience rain and thunderstorms in the afternoon, before conditions clear up with no rain expected by nightfall. - Bernama
